jobs.title: THECB - Director of IT Operations (ITS)
jobs.description:
About the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board

The Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board (THECB) works to ensure that all Texans have access to high-quality, affordable higher education opportunities that prepare students for successful careers and strengthen the state's workforce and economy. Through collaboration with colleges, universities, policymakers, and education partners across Texas, THECB advances initiatives that expand educational opportunity, promote student success, and support the future of higher education.
About Information Technology Services

The Information Technology Services (ITS) Division advances THECB's mission by delivering secure, reliable, and customer-focused technology services that enable agency staff to effectively serve Texas students, institutions, and communities.
Our organization is committed to operational excellence through modern technology, strong governance, strategic partnerships, and continuous improvement. We are modernizing how technology services are delivered by strengthening infrastructure and operational resilience, advancing cloud-first and hybrid infrastructure, improving platform reliability and security, and building a culture centered on accountability, collaboration, innovation, and service excellence.
At THECB, we believe technology is more than infrastructure and support. It is a strategic business partner that enables our agency to better serve students, institutions, and the State of Texas.
About the Role

The Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board is seeking an experienced and collaborative technology leader to serve as the Director of IT Operations. Reporting to the Senior Director of Technology, this position is a key member of the Information Technology Services leadership team and provides strategic leadership and oversight for the agency's IT operations function, including infrastructure, networks, platforms, and enterprise support systems.
The Director is responsible for ensuring the stability, performance, security, and scalability of the technology environment that enables agency business operations and advances THECB's mission, strategic priorities, and service objectives. This position establishes the strategic direction for IT operations by developing goals, objectives, operational policies, procedures, standards, service delivery practices, and performance measures that promote reliable, secure, and efficient technology operations across the agency.
Responsibilities include directing enterprise IT operations and service delivery; overseeing operational risk management, security practices, disaster recovery, and continuity planning; directing financial planning, budgeting, and cost optimization for IT operations; managing vendor relationships, service agreements, and statements of work with external service providers for infrastructure and operational support services; and providing leadership for operational governance, regulatory compliance, and organizational change.
Working collaboratively with ITS leadership, IT Service Delivery, Product Management, Product Engineering, Data Engineering, the Project Management Office (PMO), and agency stakeholders, the Director helps align operational services with business needs and long-term technology strategy while ensuring the consistent delivery of the key platforms and services that agency teams rely on.
This position supervises management and professional staff and exercises significant initiative and independent judgment while serving as a trusted advisor on IT operations, infrastructure, cloud modernization, and operational resilience.
Why Join Our Team

This is an exciting opportunity to help shape how the technology environment that supports the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board is operated, secured, and modernized.
As a member of the ITS leadership team, you'll play a critical role in advancing cloud modernization, strengthening infrastructure and security operations, improving operational resilience, and building a high-performing team focused on delivering reliable, secure, and scalable technology platforms and services.
In this role, you'll have the opportunity to:
Lead the agency's infrastructure and cloud strategy, including the move from on-premises to private and public cloud environments.
Build, mentor, and develop high-performing engineers, administrators, and managers across networking, systems, platforms, and security engineering while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
Strengthen operational resilience through disaster recovery, continuity planning, and security practices that protect agency systems and data.
Establish operational standards, service levels, and performance measures that improve reliability and support executive decision-making.
Strengthen the partnership between IT Service Delivery, Product Engineering, Data Engineering, Product Management, and the PMO to deliver the key platforms and services agency teams depend on.
Make a lasting impact by helping technology enable the agency's mission of expanding educational opportunity and supporting higher education across Texas.
If you are passionate about developing people, modernizing infrastructure, strengthening operational resilience, and building technology operations that create measurable business value, we encourage you to apply.
General Description:

Performs highly advanced (senior-level) managerial work for the Information Technology Services (ITS) Division of the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board (THECB). Serving as the Director of IT Operations, this position provides strategic leadership and oversight for the agency's IT operations function, including infrastructure, networks, platforms, and enterprise support systems. The position is responsible for ensuring the stability, performance, security, and scalability of the technology environment that enables agency business operations and advances the agency's mission, strategic priorities, and service objectives.
Work involves establishing strategic plans, goals, and objectives for IT operations; developing operational policies, procedures, standards, and service delivery practices; and establishing priorities, performance measures, and evaluation tools to assess operational effectiveness, system availability, and service quality.
Responsibilities include directing enterprise IT operations and service delivery; overseeing operational risk management, security practices, disaster recovery, and continuity planning; directing financial planning, budgeting, and cost optimization for IT operations; managing vendor relationships, service agreements, and statements of work with external service providers for infrastructure and operational support services; and providing leadership for operational governance, regulatory compliance, and organizational change. Collaborates with ITS leadership and agency stakeholders to align operational services with business needs and long-term technology strategy, and provides operational input into agency-wide planning efforts.
Supervises the work of others, including management and professional staff. Works under minimal supervision, with extensive latitude for the use of initiative and independent judgment. This position reports to the Senior Director of Technology. Performs other duties as assigned.
General Duties and Responsibilities:

Strategic People Leadership & Talent Strategy - Leads managers, senior individual contributors, or a combination of both by setting leadership expectations, supporting performance management, and guiding workforce and succession planning. Develops leadership capability and subject-matter expertise; aligns talent to strategic needs; and fosters a culture of accountability, inclusion, and continuous improvement.
Strategic Execution, Governance & Resource Alignment - Defines and oversees execution of strategies within assigned domains by establishing goals, priorities, standards, and performance measures. Aligns budgets, staffing, and resources to objectives; ensures compliance and governance; and monitors organizational performance to achieve agency outcomes.
IT Operations & Service Delivery Leadership - Directs enterprise IT operations and service delivery functions that support agency infrastructure, platforms, and end-user technology services. Establishes operational standards and performance expectations to ensure reliable, secure, and efficient technology services that support agency programs and mission-critical activities.
Operational Risk, Security & Continuity Management - Oversees operational practices that protect the integrity, availability, and security of enterprise technology services. Establishes standards and procedures that support operational resilience, risk mitigation, and continuity of services while ensuring alignment with regulatory requirements, internal policies, and enterprise governance expectations.
Financial, Vendor & Resource Management - Directs financial planning, budgeting, and resource allocation for IT operations. Oversees vendor relationships, contractual service agreements, and external service providers to ensure operational services are delivered efficiently and in alignment with organizational objectives and fiscal accountability standards.
Enterprise Collaboration & Operational Alignment - Collaborates with IT leadership, agency executives, and business stakeholders to align operational technology services with organizational priorities. jobs.title: Chief Information Security Officer
jobs.description:
DLA Piper is, at its core, bold, exceptional, collaborative and supportive. Our people are the backbone, heart and soul of our firm. Wherever you are in your professional journey, DLA Piper is a place you can engage in meaningful work and grow your career. Let’s see what we can achieve. Together.

Summary

The Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), working in collaboration with and in support of the firm’s strategic initiatives, is a senior executive responsible for protecting DLA Piper’s clients, people, data, reputation, and global business operations by leading a mature, business-aligned information security and cyber risk program. This role sets the strategic direction for the firm’s Information Security Management System, security governance, risk management, incident response, third-party security, data protection, and security awareness programs.

Operating as a trusted advisor to firm leadership, the Office of General Counsel, Information Technology, Information Governance, Risk Management, practice leadership, and global counterparts, the CISO ensures the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of client and firm information while enabling innovation, responsible AI adoption, operational resilience, and exceptional client service. The CISO works closely with, but independently from, the Information Technology function to provide objective risk oversight, policy leadership, executive reporting, and continuous improvement of the firm’s security posture.

Location

This position can sit in our Atlanta, Baltimore, Boston, Chicago, Miami, New York, Northern Virginia, Philadelphia, Raleigh, Short Hills, Washington D.C., or Wilmington office. Candidates must reside within a reasonable commuting distance of their assigned office and be available for periodic travel.

Responsibilities

Sets and executes the enterprise information security strategy for DLA Piper, aligning cyber risk management with firm strategy, client obligations, professional responsibility requirements, regulatory expectations, and operational resilience objectives.
Sets and executes the enterprise information security strategy for DLA Piper, aligning cyber risk management with firm strategy, client obligations, professional responsibility requirements, regulatory expectations, and operational resilience objectives.
Leads the firm’s Information Security Management System and security governance framework, including policy development, risk assessment, control monitoring, executive reporting, audit readiness, certification support, and continuous improvement.
Serves as the senior incident response leader for information security events, ensuring prompt triage, containment, investigation, evidence preservation, root-cause analysis, remediation, lessons learned, and appropriate coordination with the Office of General Counsel, firm leadership, insurers, regulators, law enforcement, vendors, and affected clients when required.
Partners with executive leadership, Information Technology, AI Innovation, AI Governance, Information Governance, Risk Management, Privacy, Procurement, Finance, Human Resources, practice leaders, and global counterparts to embed security-by-design into firm operations, technology investments, client service delivery, and major transformation initiatives.
Provides objective cyber risk advice to firm leadership and governance bodies, translating complex technical risk into clear business, legal, reputational, operational, and client-impact terms that enable timely and informed decision-making.
Oversees enterprise cyber risk identification, assessment, treatment, acceptance, and reporting, including vulnerabilities, threat intelligence, identity and access risk, cloud and infrastructure security, application security, data loss prevention, endpoint protection, email security, ransomware preparedness, and business continuity dependencies.
Leads security oversight of client and firm confidential information, including data classification, access controls, encryption, retention, secure disposal, cross-border data considerations, ethical walls, client outside counsel guidelines, and matter-specific security obligations.
Directs third-party and supplier security risk management in partnership with Procurement, Information Technology, Information Governance, and business owners, ensuring vendors that access firm or client data are assessed, monitored, and held to appropriate security, privacy, contractual, and operational standards.
Guides security review and risk oversight for emerging technologies, cloud services, legal technology, artificial intelligence, automation, analytics, and internally developed tools, ensuring innovation is deployed responsibly and in compliance with firm policies, client requirements, and applicable legal and ethical obligations.
Builds, develops, and leads a high-performing information security organization with the expertise, credibility, accountability, and service orientation required to support a complex, global, partner led professional services environment.
Defines and manages the Information Security team’s operating model, including functional roles, accountability structures, governance routines, service levels, intake and prioritization processes, escalation protocols, on-call expectations, and coordination with Information Technology, Risk, Information Governance, Privacy, Procurement, Human Resources, and practice leadership.
Recruits, develops, coaches, and retains a high-caliber Information Security team with the technical depth, risk judgment, executive presence, discretion, and client-service mindset required to operate effectively in a global law firm environment.
Sets clear goals and performance expectations for the Information Security team, regularly assesses performance against strategic objectives and operational metrics, addresses performance gaps, recognizes strong contributions, and ensures the team has the training, tools, resources, and authority needed to execute effectively.
Provides strategic, operational, and people leadership to the Information Security function, including direct and indirect leadership of security professionals, managers, analysts, advisors, vendors, and cross-functional contributors.
Defines the team’s vision, operating model, service standards, decision rights, escalation paths, and priorities to ensure the function delivers consistent, timely, risk-based, and business-aligned support across the firm. Builds a culture of accountability, confidentiality, trust, excellence, service orientation, continuous improvement, inclusion, and business partnership.
Responsible for onboarding, coaching, performance management, succession planning, professional development, retention, resource allocation, budget input, vendor oversight, and effective delegation across the security program.

Desired Skills  

Deep technical engineering expertise in technology infrastructure, Cloud, zero-trust architecture and cyber defense. Proven ability to leverage frameworks like NIST to build and operate a comprehensive defense in depth capability. Proven ability in change management, building trust with partners and transforming organizations. Experience in a global law firm, professional services firm, financial services institution, technology company, or similarly complex environment strongly preferred. Demonstrated success leading cybersecurity strategy, enterprise risk governance, incident response, regulatory and client-facing security matters, third-party risk, audit/certification programs, security awareness, and high performing teams. Experience advising senior executives, boards, managing partners, or equivalent governance bodies required.

Executive-level knowledge of cybersecurity strategy, governance, risk, compliance, privacy, data protection, incident response, threat intelligence, vulnerability management, identity and access management, cloud and network security, application security, endpoint protection, email security, encryption, logging and monitoring, disaster recovery, business continuity, third-party risk, DevSecOps, modernized secure development practices including AI SDLC, and secure technology adoption. Strong understanding of professional responsibility, client confidentiality, data classification, privilege-sensitive work, outside counsel guidelines, ethical walls, cross-border data considerations, and the security expectations of sophisticated global clients.

Demonstrated ability to translate technical risk into business and legal impact, influence senior stakeholders, lead through ambiguity, make sound risk-based decisions, and communicate with clarity, credibility, discretion, and urgency. Familiarity with ISO/IEC 27001, NIST, CIS Controls, data privacy laws, cyber insurance considerations, AI governance, and emerging legal sector cybersecurity risks strongly preferred. A leader who thrives on learning and is up to date with the fast-evolving technology landscape, especially the changing threats with the advancement of AI. Ability to not only understand security tools/needs, how these are changing but also go back to first principles in solving the underlying problems through innovation.

Demonstrate executive presence, credibility, sound judgment, and professional maturity in all interactions, particularly when advising firm leadership, senior partners, governance bodies, clients, regulators, vendors, and other high-impact stakeholders on sensitive, complex, or time-critical information security matters. Communicate with clarity, confidence, discretion, and appropriate urgency, translating complex technical, legal, operational, and risk issues into concise business terms that enable informed decisions by senior leaders and non-technical audiences. Influence senior leaders and stakeholders through trusted relationships, fact-based analysis, persuasive recommendations, and a firm-first approach that balances client expectations, legal and regulatory obligations, operational realities, risk appetite, and strategic business priorities.

Build alignment across a complex, matrixed, partner-led environment by listening effectively, anticipating concerns, managing competing perspectives, escalating appropriately, and helping leaders reach timely, defensible, and consistently supported decisions. Prepare and deliver executive-level briefings, written updates, risk narratives, Executive Committee materials, client-facing responses, and incident communications that are accurate, audience-appropriate, concise, and aligned with firm standards and confidentiality obligations. Lead difficult or sensitive conversations with diplomacy, composure, courage, and empathy, including situations involving cyber incidents, policy exceptions, risk acceptance, resource tradeoffs, control gaps, or competing leadership priorities.

Minimum Education   

Bachelor’s Degree in Information Security, Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, Business, Risk Management, Law, or a related field; equivalent senior leadership experience may be considered, where appropriate.

Preferred Education   

Master’s Degree in MBA, M.S. in Cybersecurity/Information Security, J.D., or other relevant advanced degree preferred.

Certificates

Relevant professional certifications are strongly preferred, such as CISSP, CISM, CISA, CRISC, CCISO, GIAC, ISO/IEC 27001 Lead Implementer or Lead Auditor, or comparable credentials. Demonstrated ongoing professional development in cybersecurity, privacy, risk governance, incident response, cloud security, AI governance, and legal/professional services risk is expected.

Minimum Years Of Experience  

15+ years’ progressive information security, cybersecurity, technology risk, privacy, compliance, or enterprise risk leadership experience, including significant executive-level responsibility for a complex, highly regulated, client-facing organization.

Guided by our "Fearless Pursuit of the Unexpected," we push the boundaries to achieve real business value and societal impact for clients. Zeno has also been previously recognized by the Cannes Lions International Festival of Creativity. Zeno is a DJE Holdings Company.

Job Description

SVP, AI & Technology Programs

Do you enjoy helping teams rethink how work gets done? Are you energized by guiding organizations through change, facilitating complex conversations and helping people adopt new ways of working through AI and emerging technologies?

As a SVP, AI & Technology Programs at Zeno, you will play a key role in accelerating AI adoption and business transformation across the agency. Working closely with the Head of AI & Innovation, practice leaders and client teams, you will help identify opportunities where AI can create meaningful impact, design solutions that fit real-world workflows and lead programs that drive lasting change.

This is an opportunity for a strategic and hands-on leader to shape how AI is adopted across the organization, build internal capabilities and help define the future of AI-enabled communications and client service.

The Team You're Joining

AI & Innovation is a growing team building a new practice inside a large organization. We move fast, cover a lot of ground, and hold ourselves to a high standard.

Craft over speed. Efficiency is table stakes. Everyone has the same AI tools. We take every hour AI saves and reinvest it in work that wasn't possible before. The bar is high because the stakes are high.
Build what others can't access. What separates us is the proprietary systems, methodology, and data we build in-house. We license tools when they solve the problem. But the work that differentiates Zeno is built here.
Makers who can hold a room. This role is not heads-down. You'll be facilitating workshops with client teams, presenting to senior leadership, and sitting across from practitioners who need you to understand their work before you prescribe anything. We look for people who are strong technically and equally comfortable communicating what they know to people who don't share their vocabulary.

About The Role

AI Transformation & Program Leadership: Lead workflow transformation programs across Zeno's offices, helping teams identify opportunities to improve how work gets done through AI, automation and emerging technologies.
Workshop Facilitation & Change Management: Facilitate working sessions with teams and stakeholders to map workflows, identify opportunities for improvement and drive alignment around solutions, ownership and implementation plans.
AI Enablement & Training: Design and deliver training programs, workshops and best practices that help employees build confidence, strengthen capabilities and adopt AI-powered ways of working.
Technology Evaluation & Adoption: Evaluate AI tools, platforms and vendor solutions, providing recommendations based on business needs, workflow impact and long-term organizational value.
AI Adoption & Organizational Effectiveness: Monitor adoption, identify barriers and refine programs that drive lasting behavioral change and measurable outcomes.
Client Innovation & Strategic Guidance: Support client teams in AI-related conversations, helping navigate usage standards, implementation considerations and opportunities to enhance client work through AI-enabled solutions.
Governance & Cross-Agency Collaboration: Help ensure AI tools and workflows align with company policies, responsible AI practices and data privacy requirements while partnering with sister agencies on shared initiatives and learning opportunities.

Exceptional communication and presentation skills, with the ability to translate complex technologies into clear, actionable recommendations that build confidence and trust.

new_jobs.description:
CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Built for pioneers by pioneers, CoreWeave delivers a platform of technology, tools, and teams that enables innovators to build and scale AI with confidence. Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability. Founded in 2017, CoreWeave became a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CRWV) in March 2025. Learn more at www.coreweave.com.

What You'll Do

You'll join CoreWeave's Global Security & Resilience organization to build and drive the security program supporting our rapidly expanding international footprint — including offices we operate directly and locations where we support our data center teams. You'll work closely with executive protection, the GSOC, External Affairs, and cross-functional business leaders to protect our people and operations as CoreWeave scales globally.

The Staff Security Program Manager, International Security will own and drive CoreWeave's international security program, with responsibility for global travel security, international office and site protection, global security partnerships and outreach, and support for executive protection and event security as needed. You'll partner closely with CoreWeave's Senior Manager, Corporate Security, who leads the domestic program, to coordinate standards, incident response, and shared protective operations.

This individual contributor role combines enterprise program ownership with hands-on operational execution. You'll design and stand up a world-class travel security program — pre-travel risk assessments, traveler tracking and duty-of-care protocols, in-country support, and emergency response for employees traveling or working abroad. You'll also establish security standards for CoreWeave's growing international office footprint and the locations where CoreWeave supports its data center teams, in partnership with Facilities, Data Center Operations, and local leadership.

A significant part of this role is external-facing: building and sustaining global partnerships with law enforcement, intelligence services, diplomatic security, industry peers, and trusted local security providers in the countries where CoreWeave operates. You'll also provide tactical, hands-on support for executive protection and event security as needed — including advances, logistics coordination, and on-the-ground protective coverage — both domestically and internationally.

Success in this role requires strategic thinking, cultural fluency, and sound judgment operating in ambiguous, fast-moving international environments. You must be comfortable building programs from the ground up, influencing stakeholders without direct authority, working through a network of internal teams, contractors, and in-country partners, and delivering results with limited on-the-ground infrastructure. This role has no direct reports.

About The Role

Design, build, and own CoreWeave's global travel security program, including pre-travel risk assessments, country risk ratings, traveler tracking, duty-of-care protocols, and coordination of 24/7 emergency response and evacuation support for employees traveling or working abroad.
Develop and maintain security standards, governance, and risk assessments for CoreWeave's international office footprint and the locations where CoreWeave supports its data center teams, balancing consistent global controls with local risk, culture, and regulatory requirements.
Build and sustain global partnerships and outreach with foreign law enforcement, intelligence, diplomatic security, and industry security counterparts, as well as trusted in-country guard force, investigative, and protective service providers.
Serve as CoreWeave's primary international security point of contact for new-market entry and international office openings, conducting site and country risk assessments and coordinating security coverage ahead of business expansion.
Drive program execution across internal teams, regional security partners, and contracted providers, establishing clear requirements, coordinating deliverables, and evaluating provider performance.
Personally plan and provide tactical, hands-on support for executive protection and high-profile event security as needed, including advances, route and venue assessments, logistics coordination, and on-site protective coverage domestically and abroad.
Translate threat, political, and protective intelligence into practical guidance for travelers, international offices, and business leaders, including country and regional travel advisories.
Coordinate with the GSOC, the domestic Corporate Security team, and internal response teams to ensure seamless monitoring, escalation, and incident management for international employees, offices, and events.
Develop budget recommendations, manage approved international security program spend, and oversee the vendor and travel-security-provider portfolio and technology roadmap, including traveler tracking and mass-notification tools.
Advise senior leaders and cross-functional partners in People, Legal, Real Estate, and Data Center Operations on international security risk and risk-informed business decisions.
Establish metrics to evaluate program effectiveness, traveler safety outcomes, partner performance, and risk reduction across the international portfolio, and use findings to drive program improvements.

Who You Are

You have 10+ years of experience across international security, travel risk management, executive protection, or protective intelligence — ideally including government, law enforcement, military, or corporate security experience with an international or liaison component.
You have direct, hands-on experience building or running a corporate travel security program, including risk assessments, traveler tracking, and emergency response for employees traveling internationally.
You have demonstrated the ability to independently own complex programs, establish priorities, and drive cross-functional results through expertise and influence.
You have experience building relationships with foreign law enforcement, intelligence, diplomatic security, or international corporate security partners, and are comfortable operating across cultures and time zones.
You have direct, hands-on experience supporting executive protection operations, including advance work, route and venue assessments, and on-site protective coverage.
You have experience assessing security requirements for new international offices, sites, or markets, ideally including facilities that support data center or critical infrastructure operations.
You can move effectively between strategic program ownership and hands-on operational execution, including personally deploying when circumstances require.
You demonstrate a high degree of discretion, judgment, integrity, and composure when working with sensitive information and high-stakes, cross-border situations.
You possess strong planning, communication, and cross-cultural relationship-building skills, and can operate independently in high-pressure or time-sensitive situations.
You are willing and able to travel internationally up to 50% to support office openings, travel security operations, partnership building, and executive protection or event assignments.

Preferred

Prior experience in federal law enforcement, the military, the intelligence community, diplomatic security, or professional protective services, particularly with international liaison or overseas assignments.
Experience building international security or investigative partnerships — for example, establishing joint programs, liaison relationships, or capacity-building initiatives with foreign law enforcement or partner agencies.
Experience building or owning security programs supporting rapid international expansion, in environments with ambiguity, limited local infrastructure, and evolving operating models.
Familiarity with data center, colocation, or other critical infrastructure security requirements in an international context.
Foreign language proficiency and demonstrated cultural fluency operating across multiple regions.
Experience managing international security program budgets, travel-security or intelligence vendors, and technology platforms supporting traveler safety.

Requirements

Wondering if you're a good fit?
We believe in investing in our people and value the unique perspectives that diversified experiences bring to our teams—even if you don't meet 100% of the listed requirements. If the following qualities describe you, we'd love to start a conversation:

You love building security programs from the ground up that scale with a rapidly growing international footprint
You are just as comfortable personally running an executive protection detail or advance as you are building a partnership with a foreign law enforcement agency
You are experienced translating threat and risk intelligence into real-world decisions for travelers and offices around the world
You are an expert at building trust and coordinating across teams, cultures, and partners to deliver practical security outcomes, often with limited resources

Why CoreWeave?

About

At CoreWeave, we work hard, have fun, and move fast. We are in an era of hyper-growth, and we invite you to be part of the journey. We embrace complexity, foster continuous learning, and care deeply about both what we build and how we work together. Our culture is defined by our core values:

Be Curious at Your Core: Always seeking better ways to solve problems.
Act Like an Owner: Taking initiative and being accountable for our collective success.
Empower Employees: Supporting independent thinking and entrepreneurial outlooks.
Deliver Best-in-Class Client Experiences: Putting excellence at the heart of every interaction.
Achieve More Together: Believing that collaboration leads to innovative solutions.

You will be surrounded by the industry's best talent, working in an environment that encourages independent thinking and rewards innovation. As our organization expands, so do your opportunities for growth. Come join us and turn compute into capability.
